extracted.intended_audience: scholars and authors submitting articles to the Stanford Law Review 2026 Symposium on administrative law
extracted.subtask_description: Call-for-papers and submission rules for articles to be considered for the Stanford Law Review 2026 Symposium (The APA at Eighty). Covers topical scope, submission process, review standards, publication conditions, and conference participation requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manuscript submission method
rubrics_metrics.description: Please submit your manuscript through the Scholastica submissions portal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors must use Scholastica to submit their manuscript; after submitting via Scholastica, send a message indicating interest in the symposium (see 'Indicate interest' criterion).

rubrics_metrics.name: Indicate interest in being considered for the Symposium
rubrics_metrics.description: To be considered for our symposium, please send a short message via email to articles@stanfordlawreview.org indicating your interest after submitting your manuscript through Scholastica.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submitting via Scholastica alone is not the signal for symposium consideration — authors should separately notify the Volume 78 Senior Articles Editor (or indicate via Scholastica) that they wish to be considered for the symposium.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anonymous/blind review and standard editorial requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Articles considered for symposium undergo the same anonymous review process and receive consideration along the same editorial standards (including word count) as any other article submitted to SLR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions must conform to Stanford Law Review's standard editorial expectations (including its word count limits); symposium consideration does not change the blind-review process or editorial standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topical relevance: administrative law and executive power
rubrics_metrics.description: SLR is particularly enthusiastic about pieces touching on administrative law and executive power for inclusion in our 2026 Symposium, The APA at Eighty: What’s Next for Administrative Law?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions should engage topics related to the APA, administrative law generally, or executive power; relevance to the symposium theme is a key dimension of selection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted approaches and subject-matter modes
rubrics_metrics.description: SLR invites authors to submit manuscripts that address doctrinal, historical, empirical, or normative aspects of administrative law generally or specific areas of administration (e.g., environmental law, immigration law, national security).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors may use doctrinal analysis, historical research, empirical methods, or normative/critical approaches; pieces focusing on specific regulatory areas are welcome so long as they connect to administrative law themes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suggested research questions and sample topics
rubrics_metrics.description: Sample topics include, but are by no means limited to: What remains of the APA’s vision of the regulatory state? What has been the impact of the APA? What is the proper role of judicial review? Do the Major Questions or Non-Delegation Doctrines apply to national security or immigration in the same way they apply to environmental or securities regulation? Are developments trans-substantive or limited to particular areas? How might historical sources improve understandings? What role can state/local regulators play? What are the justice implications of recent decisions? What impact might we expect from recent and upcoming decisions (Loper Bright, Corner Post, Jarkesy, San Francisco v. EPA, Calumet Shreveport Refining, Wages & White Lion Investments, VanDerStok, Eagle County)? What might lower court decisions tell us about upcoming changes?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The list is illustrative — relevance to any of these questions is suitable but not required. Citing or engaging recent court decisions and their implications is encouraged where relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection outcome and publication in Volume 78
rubrics_metrics.description: All articles selected for our symposium will be published in a standard print issue of SLR. Selected manuscripts will appear in print in Volume 78 of SLR. All authors selected for the 2026 Symposium will have their pieces published in Issue Six of SLR’s Volume 78.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acceptance to the symposium carries the expectation of eventual print publication in the listed volume/issue; authors should be prepared for the work to appear in the print issue.

rubrics_metrics.name: In-person presentation as a condition of publication
rubrics_metrics.description: As a condition of publication, all authors must participate and present, in-person, at our Symposium Conference, which will likely take place in February 2026.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors selected for publication must be able to attend and present in person; inability to present in person would conflict with the stated condition of publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Travel and accommodation logistics
rubrics_metrics.description: The 2026 Symposium will take place at Stanford Law School in winter of 2026. Participants’ travel and accommodations will be provided by SLR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SLR will cover travel and lodging for participants; authors can rely on the Review to provide these arrangements should they be selected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rolling review and recommended timing
rubrics_metrics.description: The Stanford Law Review is currently accepting articles for the summer submissions cycle. We expect the cycle to be open for a couple more weeks, but we review articles on a rolling basis, so we strongly encourage authors to submit articles as soon as possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because review is rolling and the submission window may close soon, early submission is advised to maximize the chance of consideration for the symposium.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fallback consideration for general publication
rubrics_metrics.description: If your manuscript is not selected for the Symposium, it will still receive full consideration for general publication in Volume 78 of SLR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should note that symposium non-selection does not end consideration; their submission remains in the pool for standard law-review publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Questions and contact person
rubrics_metrics.description: Please submit any and all questions to Volume 78 Senior Symposium Editor, Josh Petersen, by email at jrp95@stanford.edu.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Direct procedural or substantive inquiries about submission or the symposium to the named Senior Symposium Editor.
